limitations: The positive base rate rises over time - 45.5 percent in train, 74.0 in evaluation, 72.2 in holdout - because the free-allocation share fell while the cap declined. Read every score against the documented per-year prevalence.

The single column margin_t alone reaches an AUC near 0.90 under the gate's one-column sweep: the intended one-line rule nearly solves the task, so a model must beat it honestly rather than rediscover it.
Exact emission-allocation ties are labelled 0 and counted (4,224 rows); the label source values are excluded from every shipped file.
The panel ends at 2025 because the extract carries no numeric verified emissions for later years at the snapshot date.

No claim of real-time or operational forecasting validity: historical feature and label availability at the prediction instant is assumed from a current source snapshot, not verified against release vintages.

The labeled eval split is development/validation. Final holdout scoring requires prediction-time access restrictions; the original scorer provided the complete feature frame. Downloadable holdout labels must stay outside model development.

paragraphs: This release ships 188,205 installation-years from the EU emissions trading system, covering compliance years 2006 through 2025. The panel is built from the European Commission's Union Registry public extracts: 617,448 rows over 23,748 installations across 32 registries, restricted to the years where both the year's allocation and the previous year's emissions are known.

The intended decision point is 30 April of compliance year t, using prior-year emissions and year-t allocation. Those values come from current registry extracts; this release does not verify their original publication dates, revision histories, or availability at every historical cutoff. The outcome is year-t verified emissions exceeding year-t free allocation.

The recorded baseline achieved 0.9199 validation ROC AUC under the original runner protocol, compared with a tested calendar-only rule at 0.527 and a prior-year net-position rule at 0.8671. These are comparisons with those references, not evidence that later-row access is safe or that historical availability has been verified.

The splits are temporal: train years 2006 through 2019, evaluation 2020 through 2022, holdout 2023 through 2025. The labelled holdout ships with the release and stays outside any evaluated agent's workspace.

limitations: join (installation, t) -> (installation, t+1): the next row's net_short_l1 is T's label
The labelled holdout is presumed to carry the same self-answering structure by construction; it was never opened by the audit and must be treated as compromisable by the same join class.
Historical feature/label availability at the declared instant is assumed from current snapshots, not verified against release vintages.
The current scorer passes the complete feature frame to predict_proba; prediction-time isolation is instructed but not mechanically enforced, so any framework score on these files is gameable.
